Decision and mathematics panels passed and seven cited foundations were source-attested, but D0.5 graded the completed package subfield below the field floor because of specialized scope and unresolved practical usefulness. tldr: For a randomized unit whose latent outcome law is any Borel probability measure on \([0,1]\), the causal mean contrast in ordinary unsquared Wasserstein distance to the uniform reference is indirectly measured by independent Poisson readings. With \(\ell=\log(en)\), both minimax absolute risk and finite-sample honest connected expected length have order \(n^{-1/2}+\log(e+\ell/m)/\ell\) when \(m\le\ell\), and \(n^{-1/2}+(m\ell)^{-1/2}\) when \(m>\ell\). A finite original-record polynomial and localized clipped norm procedure attains these orders and has at least ninety-percent coverage at every finite pair. The lower witnesses retain the entire count and read vector. Recruitment order for both criteria is equivalent to eventual \(m\ge b_0n/\log(en)\) for some fixed \(b_0>0\). Atoms, singular measures and mass at zero reference distance are included. Identification, abstract mixture duality and scalar magnitude approximation are credited foundations; the contribution is the explicit all-depth evaluation and certified observed-record attainment.
gap: The scalar mixture comparators and the abstract mixture modulus leave a channel-specific obligation: explicit precision for the full continuous marked-read experiment across growing depth, with finite-sample connected coverage over arbitrary density mixing.
fill: The experiment comparison identifies exactly which scalar bounds transfer. The dense finite-honesty theorem targets a public original-record construction at order \(n^{-1/2}+(m\log(en))^{-1/2}\) beyond logarithmic depth, including the recruitment-limited slice and no upper depth ceiling. The open joint-frontier and depth-growth nodes require matching full-class converses and every transition; neither is replaced by a scalar submodel.
